description.narrative: FSDAi invested into the Fund to support issuers across SSA in inclusive sectors such as MSME lending, microlending, housing, agriculture, and infrastructure.

The investment is expected to have the following effects: ▪ Mobilise domestic capital – the Fund will crowd-in local investors by acting as an anchor investor in local issuances, and never buying more than 30% of a bond. ▪ Build technical capacity – the Fund’s TA facility supports local issuers with advice and technical support to bring bonds to market, and builds the skill set, standards and practices of market intermediaries (incl. placement agents and investment banks). ▪ Market sensitisation – increasing volume of bond issuances and application of best practices will heighten awareness around the opportunity to finance through bonds and grow a nascent asset class. New best practices enhance skills and standards among intermediaries that structure and market issuances. ▪ Reduce cost of capital – for issuers, the Fund will improve their capital structure by giving them access to long-term, local currency denominated finance which gives them greater planning security and removes foreign currency exposure. ▪ Better served end-users – for clients of the issuer, the enhanced capital structure of issuers will result in better financing options for end users as issuers are able to pass on cost savings and offer more appropriate products.

This investment established by KfW in 2012 ad which sets out to address the current underdevelopment of local currency bond markets in Africa, with the objective of improving access to long-term funding for issuers as an alternative source of funding from the traditional short-term loans/overdrafts.

activity-date.narrative: - 3rd October 2017: equity - £ 7.65m - 29th May 2018: debt - £ 5m) - 11th June 2019: debt - £ 2.65m

The debt instrument will be repaid in a bullet payment after 10 years. The Fund may not prepay all or any part of the sub debt until the 5th anniversary of the first disbursement, May 2023. The Fund may prepay, after the 5th anniversary and on the interest, payment dates (15th March and 15th September) all or any part of the loan, including accrued interest, and a prepayment premium equal to 1% of the amount to be prepaid. Any amount prepaid may not be reborrowed by the Fund.
